blocks.text: Democracy is one of the most common forms of government in the world today. However, democracy is not a new form of government. Democracy has existed since ancient times, and has evolved and changed for centuries.

There are many books that have been written about democracy, both from philosophical, historical and practical perspective. However, there are five classic books that are considered the foundation of modern democratic theory. All five books are:
Republic by Plato (427-347 BC)
Politics by Aristotle (384-322 BC)
Law by Cicero (106-43 BC)
The Spirit of the Laws by Montequieu (1689-1755)
Two Treasures of Government by John Locke (1632- 1704)
Democracy as an ideal country
In his Republican book, Plato described an ideal state ruled by the philosophers. The Philosophers are people who have great knowledge and wisdom, and they will lead the country fairly and wisely.

Plato argued that democracy was not an ideal form of government. In democracy, all citizens have the right to participate in government. However, Plato argued that many people do not have the knowledge and wisdom necessary to make the right decision about how to rule the country.
Aristotle: Democracy as a mixed form of government

Aristotle argued that democracy was a good form of government, but only if it was balanced by other forms of government. Aristotle believed that an ideal form of government was a mixed form of government, which combines the unsurahs of various forms of government, including democracy, monarchy and aristocracy.
Aristotle argued that democracy had some advantages, including:
Democracy allows all citizens to participate in the government.
Democracy drives to equality and justice.
Democracy can produce a fair and wise leader.
But Aristotle also realized that democracy has some flaws, including:
Democracy can lead to bad decisions, if made by people who don't have the necessary knowledge and wisdom.
Democracy can be susceptible to demargogi, which is the use of interesting speeches to fool people.
Democracy is the best form of government.

Cicero argued that democracy was the best form of government, because it allowed all citizens to participate in government. Cicero believes that the participation of citizens is important to ensure that the government goes fairly and wisely.
Cicero argued that democracy had some advantages, including:
Democracy allows all citizens to voice their opinion.
Democracy drives to equality and justice.
Democracy can produce a fair and wise leader.
Montesquieu: Democracy as a stable form of government

Montesquieu argued that democracy is the most stable form of government, if balanced with systems checks and balances. Montesquieu believes that systems check and balances are required to prevent power from becoming too centered in one hand.
Montesquieu argued that democracy had some advantages, including:
Democracy allows all citizens to participate in the government.
Democracy drives to equality and justice.
Democracy can produce a fair and wise leader.
Locke: Democracy is a form of government that protects human rights
Locke argued that all humans have natural rights, including the right to live, freedom, and ownership. These rights, according to him, can only be protected by democratic governments.
Locke argued that democracy had some advantages, including:
Democracy allows all citizens to protect their rights.
Democracy drives to equality and justice.
Democracy can produce a fair and wise leader.
Conclusion
These five classic books have contributed significant to modern democratic theories. The books have helped develop our understanding of democracy, including:
The definition of democracy.
The principles of democracy.
Overkill and lack of democracy.
These books have also helped inspire revolution and democratic reform around the world.
Doctor. Hanny Per, MBA
